content.user_title: Map Conversion Values for Profit-Based Bidding
content.value_statement: Revenue-based bidding can favor sales that produce little profit. This skill maps margin-adjusted values and defensible proxies, then checks launch readiness.
actual_capabilities: Classifies conversion actions as revenue-bearing or non-revenue.
Maps revenue to net value using supplied margin or COGS data.
Derives proxy values from net order value and close rates.
Compares static values, dynamic values, and segmented value rules.
Reconciles platform conversion value against booked business contribution.
Produces a value-model specification, QA sheet, and launch-readiness decision.
limitations: Does not verify whether conversion tags fire or whether tracking parameters are correct.
Does not resolve cross-platform attribution, duplicate orders, or incrementality.
Cannot derive reliable values without revenue, margin, COGS, or close-rate inputs.
Does not change advertising accounts or publish platform value rules.

use_cases.title: Prepare a tROAS Relaunch
use_cases.description: Convert product revenue into margin-adjusted values and identify blockers before restoring value-based bidding.

use_cases.title: Validate Ecommerce Profit Signals
use_cases.description: Compare category margins, transaction values, and platform totals against booked contribution.

use_cases.title: Value Lead Conversions
use_cases.description: Derive lead, call, and signup proxies from close rates and expected net order value.

prompt_templates.title: Inventory Conversion Actions
prompt_templates.prompt: List my conversion actions and classify each as revenue-bearing or non-revenue. Ask for missing inputs before assigning values.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start a new value model with a clear inventory.

prompt_templates.title: Map Purchase Profit
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a profit-based purchase value model from my revenue and category margin data. Label every value by evidence source.
prompt_templates.scenario: Replace gross revenue with contribution-based values.

prompt_templates.title: Derive Proxy Values
prompt_templates.prompt: Derive proxy values for leads, calls, and signups using close rates and net order value. Mark missing inputs clearly.
prompt_templates.scenario: Value conversions that have no direct transaction revenue.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Launch Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this conversion value model for double adjustments, value-count mismatch, and launch blockers. Recommend one next action.
prompt_templates.scenario: Review a complete model before value-based bidding begins.

output_examples.input: Purchases have dynamic revenue. Category margins are 30 percent and 55 percent.
output: Use dynamic transaction revenue as the starting value.
Apply the matching category margin to calculate net value.
Keep unmatched categories blocked until a margin is supplied.

output_examples.input: Average net order value is 120 dollars and lead close rate is 10 percent.
output_examples.output: Set the estimated lead proxy to 12 dollars. Label the value as derived from net order value and close rate.

output_examples.input: Platform value totals 300,000 dollars while booked contribution is 100,000 dollars.
output_examples.output: The reconciliation fails at three times booked contribution. Check duplicate adjustments, gross revenue inputs, and counted conversion actions before launch.

best_practices: Provide recent exports with clear dates, currencies, and conversion names.
Use product or category margins when profitability varies materially.
Label each value as measured, user-provided, estimated, or needs-input.
anti_patterns: Do not present guessed margins or round proxy values as facts.
Do not apply a value rule to data already adjusted for the same factor.
Do not launch when platform value and booked contribution remain materially unreconciled.

faq.question: Does this skill verify conversion tracking?
faq.answer: No. It models conversion values after tracking behavior has been verified.

faq.question: Can it work with gross revenue only?
faq.answer: Yes, but the result cannot represent profit until margin or COGS data is supplied.

faq.question: How are lead values calculated?
faq.answer: It multiplies expected net order value by the measured or user-provided close rate.

faq.question: Does it support static and dynamic values?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends the simplest model supported by transaction variability and available data.

faq.question: Will it update my advertising account?
faq.answer: No. It produces a specification and QA results for review and implementation.

faq.question: Can it resolve duplicate attribution across platforms?
faq.answer: No. Cross-platform attribution and duplicate order reconciliation require a separate workflow.
